samples.summary: Author-only edit/delete gate is enforced only on the REST path; the Yorkie CRDT is a second writer with no equivalent server-side check, so a session-authenticated user can still edit or delete another user's comment
samples.evidence:
`assertCommentAuthor` (comments.controller.ts:519-534) is the only server-side enforcement of the "edit / delete by author only" rule, and its docblock (lines 106-110, 508-517) claims it exists because "the editor is no longer the only writer" and that without it "any member of a workspace could delete anybody's comment". The gate covers only `PATCH/DELETE /api/v1/.../comments/...`. The comment threads it protects live entirely inside the Yorkie CRDT (`root.comments` / `sheets[tabId].comments`), and the CRDT is directly writable by browser clients over the collaboration channel.

Bypassing call site: `YorkieAuthController.hasAccess`, packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:196-206 — "Membership grants read+write; the model has no per-member viewer role today". Any workspace member can therefore mint a Yorkie token (`GET /auth/yorkie-token`, auth.controller.ts:68-73) , attach `doc-<id>` / `pdf-<id>` / `sheet-<id>` read-write, and run `doc.update(root => { delete root.comments[threadId] })` or rewrite `root.comments[t].comments[i].body` from the browser console — deleting or silently editing another member's comment with no authorship check anywhere. The frontend gate (`CommentThreadCard.tsx`) is client-side only.

Amplifier: the auth webhook ships in shadow mode by default (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` unset → `this.enforce = false`, yorkie-auth.controller.ts:100-119; documented default `false` in packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:185). In shadow mode every computed deny is turned into an allow, so in a stock deployment the CRDT path is not authorized at all — any holder of any valid Yorkie token (including a share-link visitor whose token names a different document) can attach to an arbitrary document key and rewrite its comments.

Mitigation that keeps this at major rather than critical: `/auth/yorkie-token` is `JwtAuthGuard`-only, so an API-key caller (the population these routes exist for) genuinely cannot reach the CRDT path, and the REST gate does bind it. The delta under review adds tests that assert this gate holds for `doc`/`pdf`, which makes the surface read as covered; the gate should be documented as advisory-for-interactive-sessions, or the rule needs to move somewhere the CRDT writer also passes through.

samples.summary: The new mutating v1 controller (`ApiV1CommentsController`) was not added to the `ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard` mount-coverage test that the repo maintains specifically to stop an ungated mutating v1 route
samples.evidence: api-key-write-scope.guard.spec.ts:59-78 states its own purpose: "Enumerating the controllers here is what stops the next v1 controller from reintroducing it: a new mutating route is covered the moment its controller carries the guard, and this test fails if one does not." The enumerated list is docs-content, documents, files, folders, images, tabs, cells. This PR adds `ApiV1CommentsController` with four mutating routes (POST thread, POST reply, PATCH resolve/edit, DELETE thread/comment) and it is absent from that list. No exploit today — comments.controller.ts:113 does mount `CombinedAuthGuard, WorkspaceScopeGuard, ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard`, so a read-scoped API key is refused — but the regression protection the repo relies on does not extend to the new controller, so a later refactor that drops the decorator (letting a read-only API key write comments and fire notifications) would pass CI silently. Note the list is already stale for worksheet*/slides controllers, which is how the gap arose.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claimed chain checks out in the repository. `assertCommentAuthor` (comments.controller.ts:519-534) is the only server-side enforcement of "edit/delete by author only", invoked solely from the REST handlers at lines 431, 463 and 502, and its docblock (507-518) explicitly frames itself as the server-side counterpart to the client-side editor gate. The same comment data is directly writable by browser clients over the CRDT: yorkie-comment-store.ts:158-265 performs `doc.update` on `root.comments[threadId]`, rewrites `t.comments[i].body` (237-241) and `delete root.comments![threadId]` (252). The only server-side authorization on that path is the Yorkie auth webhook, and `hasAccess` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:188-207) grants any workspace member document-wide read+write with no authorship notion ("Membership grants read+write; the model has no per-member viewer role today"). Tokens are mintable by any session user at auth.controller.ts:68-73. The shadow-mode amplifier is also real: enforce defaults to false (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:100-101) and every computed deny is converted to an allow (111-119), with the documented default `false` at packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:185 and the same caveat acknowledged in packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:40-42 and packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4322-4325 — so in a stock deployment even a share-link visitor's token can attach to an arbitrary document key and rewrite comments. The frontend gate is client-side only (CommentThreadCard.tsx:89-92). No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, no guard elsewhere covers the CRDT writer, and an authorization rule enforced on only one of two writer paths is squarely in the access-control lane of this lens.
